subject: Dedicated capacity: pre-commit GPU footprint clarification for Axion Labs
messages:
From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@axionlabs.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated sizing validation before commit

Diego —

Thanks for taking this. We're about to finalize the reserved capacity commit for Q1 but want a quick sanity check on the GPU footprint before we lock numbers in procurement. Below is our current traffic profile — pulled from prod telemetry (attached). Can you confirm whether that aligns with a Dedicated plan capacity estimate, and if there are obvious levers (caching / model precision) you recommend to reduce committed GPUs?

High level:
- Monthly requests: ~1,020,000 (mostly API-based calls from our inference gateway)
- Prompt / response average tokens: prompt 85 tokens (median 60), response 420 tokens (median 300)
- Workload mix: chat-style completions 40%, long-form summarization 35% (responses often 800+ tokens), code generation 25% (bursty, heavy decoding)
- Typical sustained QPS: 8–12; observed peak-burst QPS: 110 (bursts last ~7–12 minutes, 2–4 bursts/day, concentrated in US morning hours)
- Session behavior: users often keep an open session for multi-turn chat for ~6 minutes on average; KV cache hit measured at ~28% on prefixes we control
- Latency requirement: goal is p95 < 350ms for chat responses; long-form summarization can tolerate higher p95 but we want p99 < 3s global

Constraints / asks:
1) We'd prefer a quantized 70B-class model variant if that materially reduces GPUs vs 70B fp16.
2) We'd like example sizing options (conservative / baseline / aggressive) with assumptions called out (batching, session affinity, KV cache hit-rate).
3) Any suggestions to flatten bursts (prefetching, rate-limiting patterns) that would reduce commitment are welcome.

Attached: axion_token_profile.csv (token histogram + hourly QPS). Happy to jump on a 20–30 min call if helpful.

—Liam
CTO, Axion Labs

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@axionlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing validation before commit

Liam —

Appreciate the profile and the attachment, this is exactly the kind of signal we need. Quick clarifying questions so our first-pass sizing doesn't wander:

1) Model variant: are you targeting a specific model (e.g., Llama-2-70b, Mistral-70b) and do you have a preference between int8 / int4 quantized builds vs fp16? That changes per-GPU throughput a lot.
2) KV cache expectations: your note about ~28% prefix hit is helpful — is that measured after applying your own application-level prefix caching, or is it observed at the LLM cache level?
3) Session affinity: do you require strict session-to-GPU affinity (sticky) for multi-turn? If not, we can use short-lived sessions and reduce warm KV cache overhead.
4) SLO targets: p50/p95/p99 targets for each workload type (chat / summarization / code) — you mentioned p95 < 350ms for chat and p99 < 3s for long-form; can we confirm p50 targets?

I'll put together a three-option sizing (conservative / baseline / cost-optimized) once we get those answers. I'm attaching a short pre-commit sizing form that helps us plug your telemetry into a simulation. If you can return the token histogram + a daypart QPS sample (morning/afternoon/evening), we can run a simulated burst with real decoding characteristics.

Attachment: precommit_sizing_form.pdf

If it's easier, I'll schedule a 25-min sync and loop Marissa in for the capacity estimates.

Best,
Diego
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@axionlabs.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing validation before commit

Liam / Diego —

Copied in with a quick internal first-pass estimate based on the numbers Diego provided. This is not final but should help frame procurement conversations. Assumptions called out inline.

Summary (first-pass):
- Workload mix and token counts imply high decoding cost because long-form summarization and code paths dominate token output.
- If we assume a quantized 70B int8-like runtime and conservative KV cache hit of 30% (matches your ~28%), we estimate baseline sustained throughput per A100-80GB-equivalent GPU: ~30–40 inference tokens/sec effective for mixed requests (after batching benefits). For A10/A30-class GPUs those numbers drop and latency SLOs are harder to meet for p95.

Sizing options (rough):
- Conservative (SLO-first): 32 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs reserved. Rationale: meets p95 < 350ms for chat and p99 < 3s for long-form with room for two simultaneous bursts.
- Baseline (cost + SLO mix): 24 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs. Uses aggressive batching and prioritized burst credits; will satisfy average-day SLAs but may see higher p99 under compounded bursts.
- Cost-optimized (risk-tolerant): 18 x A100-80GB-equivalent GPUs + burst capacity and higher reliance on prefix caching (~40% target). This reduces commitment but risks tail latency during heavy multi-turn sessions.

Key levers that materially change sizing:
- Model precision: switching from fp16 to int8/int4 typically improves effective tokens/sec by 1.7–2x on the same hardware (high-impact).
- KV cache hit-rate: moving from 28% -> 45% reduces decoding token volume and can drop required GPUs by ~20–25%.
- Burst smoothing: introducing short prefetch or user-side rate-limit (e.g., queueing 2–5s windows) flattens peak and improves batching efficiency.

Next steps we recommend:
1) Confirm model family + quantization target (int8/int4 vs fp16).
2) Provide a CSV histogram with token counts by request (if you can, the attached axion_token_histogram_v2.csv helps).
3) Approve a short simulation run: we can ingest your sample traffic and run a 90-minute stress sim (synthetic) to validate p95/p99 tail under the 110 QPS burst pattern.

If you want, we can attach a cost delta table comparing A100 vs later-generation accelerators and show committed-month price differences.

—Marissa
Principal Capacity Planner, Redwood Inference

From: Liam O'Neal <liam.oneal@axionlabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Dec 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing validation before commit

Thanks both — this is super helpful. Quick answers:
- Model: Leaning to Llama-2-70b quantized (int8) for a first pass. We can test int4 later if stable.
- KV cache: the 28% number is measured at the application layer (we keep user history prefixes server-side), so some additional hit is possible if Redwood applies model-side prefix canonicalization.
- Session: would prefer soft affinity — best-effort to keep session tokens local but not strict, so fallbacks are acceptable.
- p50 targets: chat p50 < 120ms, summarization p50 < 800ms, code p50 < 400ms.

I'll upload the token histogram and a 48-hour daypart CSV to the Drive link you shared. Please go ahead with the 90-minute stress sim against the quantized 70B profile and return the sim report — we'll use that to finalize the commitment.

Attachment: axion_token_histogram_v2.csv (uploaded).

Liam
CTO, Axion Labs
